answer: Each identity registers a lotus beacon post, locks 80 credits as bond, and pays a fee. Each epoch the auditor flashes distinct lotus codes on a horizon board at once. Each identity must reply with its code plus a nectar tag; the auditor checks the registry and publishes timestamps. A missed or duplicated reply burns the bond and voids the identity. The kth filing costs 35+7(k-1): the 1000th costs 7028, so 1000 fakes cost 3,531,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-response ring fails because one operator cannot answer two codes at once. An honest agent pays 35 once, then recovers it.
